cases.query: How does Flask load application settings from a Python file on disk?
cases.why: 'settings' hints variable, but the loader is Config.from_pyfile, a method (config.py:187) that execs the file as a module and copies uppercase attrs via from_object.

cases.query: How do you turn a class-based view into a plain view function you can pass to add_url_rule?
cases.why: 'class-based' hints class, but the conversion is done by View.as_view, a classmethod (views.py:86) that returns a closure named 'view' registrable as a route function.

cases.query: Where does Flask keep the shared type aliases used for response and header values across its modules?
cases.why: 'type aliases' hints class, but these are plain module-level type aliases defined in typing.py (e.g. ResponseValue, HeadersValue), and the only indexed symbol is the module itself, kind=module.

cases.query: How does Flask make sure request-scoped cleanup code still runs even when the view raised an exception during dispatch?
cases.why: Flask.do_teardown_request (app.py:1423) runs all teardown_request callbacks and the request_tearing_down signal right before the request context pops, passing the exception if dispatch failed, per do_teardown_request's docstring at app.py:1423-1453.

cases.query: How can code register something to run and tweak the response right after the current request finishes, without affecting other requests?
cases.why: after_this_request (ctx.py:118) appends the given callable to ctx._after_request_functions so it only runs for the current request, unlike Scaffold.after_request which applies to every request.

cases.query: How does Flask turn the signed cookie sent by the browser back into the session dictionary at the start of a request, falling back to an empty session if the signature is invalid?
cases.why: SecureCookieSessionInterface.open_session (sessions.py:323) reads the cookie value, verifies it with the signing serializer, and returns an empty SecureCookieSession on missing cookie or BadSignature.

cases.query: What allows work started in a new thread from inside a view to keep seeing the same request and app data that were active in that view, since new threads don't automatically pick this up?
cases.why: copy_current_request_context (ctx.py:154) captures the active context and wraps the decorated callable to push a copy of it before running, so background threads/greenlets see the same request/app data.

cases.query: How does Flask serve a single uploaded file from inside a directory while blocking a client-supplied filename from escaping outside that directory?
cases.why: send_from_directory (helpers.py:543) docstring states it uses werkzeug.security.safe_join to ensure the client-supplied path cannot point outside the given directory before delegating to send_file.

cases.query: What is the method that reads configuration values from environment variables sharing a common prefix?
cases.why: Config.from_prefixed_env (config.py:126) loads env vars starting with a given prefix (default FLASK_), strips the prefix, and sets them as config keys; kind=method matches the explicit 'method' noun.

cases.query: What is the class that holds the temporary registration state used while a blueprint is being attached to an application?
cases.why: BlueprintSetupState (sansio/blueprints.py:34) docstring calls itself 'a temporary holder object for registering a blueprint with the application'; kind=class matches the explicit 'class' noun.

cases.query: What is the function that converts a view's return value into a proper response object you can then attach headers to?
cases.why: helpers.make_response (helpers.py:151) is the module-level convenience function whose docstring describes converting a view's return value into a Response so headers can be attached; kind=function matches the explicit 'function' noun.

cases.query: What is the method that determines the correct exception class and status code to use when handling a given error identifier?
cases.why: Scaffold._get_exc_class_and_code (sansio/scaffold.py:665) resolves an int HTTP code or Exception subclass to (exc_class, code), used when registering/looking up error handlers; kind=method matches the explicit 'method' noun.
